---
title: Meet standalone Cloudflare release
description: Qualify and publish an exact main commit with a captured rollback pair.
---

Meet can publish independently through `meet-cloudflare.yaml`. A release dispatch
must use the `main` ref and supply its full 40-character commit as `source_sha`.
The workflow rejects a mismatch between that input and `github.sha`; a moving
branch cannot silently select another release candidate.

Build identity acceptance requires the Meet app name, exact source SHA, production
environment, and production ref name. A mismatch reports only allowlisted identity
fields and valid source hashes; arbitrary response bodies are excluded. Compare
that receipt with the sealed artifact before attributing a failure to caching or
propagation. The restored production runtime checks the same identity fields before
publication. A failed promotion restores the captured pair and requires fresh
release authorization before another dispatch or rerun.

## Prepare the release

The existing `meet-production` GitHub environment must permit exactly the
`production` and `main` branches and require approval by `vhpx` before dispatch.
Both the train and standalone deploy jobs use this protected environment. Its
existing secrets remain unchanged. Environment policy changes require the release
authority's approval and execution by the credential custodian. Verify the policy
readback before dispatch; a missing environment must never be auto-created by a
release run. Never copy secret values into logs, command arguments, review packets
or run artifacts.

When the repository variable `MEET_DEDICATED_PRODUCTION_ENV_READY` is `true`, both
deploy paths use the dedicated `meet-cloudflare-production` environment instead,
because Parley also deploys through `meet-production`. It needs the same branch
policy and reviewer, plus `MEET_DEDICATED_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`,
`MEET_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET` and `PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`; the dedicated
path has no shared or account-level Cloudflare token fallback. Approve that
environment's pending deployment in the steps below while the variable is set.

Record the exact candidate, live-to-candidate source-range review, current release
holds and provider authorization. The candidate must include the accepted startup
and authentication regression fixes. A source review or green build does not
replace the per-dispatch authorization or source-range receipt.

The admission gate evaluates only checks relevant to Meet. Security Checks and
Meet Cloudflare need the latest completed successful run for the exact main SHA.
Type Check, Test and Oxc are repository-wide and check the whole tree when they
execute. The exact SHA's green run counts. Otherwise the nearest green run of
that workflow on an ancestor commit (at most 200 commits back) counts when no
relevant file changed between the two commits and that run's own jobs show its
checks executed rather than skipping: Type Check's `Run type check` step, every
Test unit shard plus the root script tests, and both Oxc jobs. Release-only and
release-merge pushes conclude green with those skipped, so they never count. Relevant files are `apps/meet` and every workspace it depends on,
paths those files reference by relative specifier (for example
`scripts/ci/meet-native-policy.mjs`), root files, `.github/actions`, `patches`
and the checking workflow itself. Descendant commits never count, because a
later green run may have skipped its checks. A red or superseded run caused
only by another app therefore does not block Meet; any relevant change still
needs the exact SHA's green run. The receipt records the equivalent commit
(`equivalentSha`) and its distance. The logic lives in
`scripts/ci/release-relevant-ci.mjs`. It relies on those three workflows
checking the whole tree on main pushes even when the CI planner
(`scripts/ci/ci-plan.mjs`) narrows pull requests;
`scripts/ci/release-relevant-ci-plan.test.mjs` fails if a main push could
narrow Type Check, Test shards or Oxc.

CodeQL is not a release gate. Its diff-scoped main push scan and the nightly
full scan surface new high or critical results without holding a release; an
open high or critical finding still holds the release under the security
default. The gate excludes the current release run. A successful Meet workflow
whose `validate` job was skipped by the affected-path gate counts as green for
this historical CI predicate. It is not an emitted-artifact qualification
receipt: the release dispatch must execute its own validation, restored-artifact
checks and production-input provenance.

## Dispatch and approve

After the exact commit is on main and the release packet is approved:

```sh
gh workflow run meet-cloudflare.yaml --ref main \
  -f release=true -f source_sha="$SOURCE_SHA"
```

Record the resulting run ID and confirm its `head_sha` matches the approved
candidate. The reviewer approves only that run's pending
`meet-production` deployment, after the release authority issues a provider ACK
naming that run ID and the reviewer checks the candidate. If main advances before dispatch, the SHA equality guard stops the
run; qualify the new candidate instead of changing the input silently.

Both release paths use the fixed `meet-cloudflare-production-deploy` concurrency
group. Admission repeats inside that group before provider operations. For a
production-ref run, live equal to or descended from the source is a successful
no-op with `MEET_RELEASE_SUPERSEDED`; it performs no deployment or success-marker
write. Divergent sources stop with `MEET_RELEASE_DIVERGENT`. A stale standalone
dispatch stops rather than replacing a newer live release.

## Artifacts and rollback

The validate job builds and seals the frontend and realtime output. Realtime's
archive SHA-256 is exported as a validate-job output and checked before extraction
in deploy, independently of the seal inside the archive. Publication uses the
qualified realtime output with `--no-bundle`; Cloudflare credentials are scoped to
provider steps, not dependency installation or compilation.

The emitted realtime Worker must include `global_fetch_strictly_public`.
Programming and document checkpoints use `PLATFORM_API_BASE_URL` or default to
`https://tuturuuu.com`. This flag sends same-zone requests through the public
platform Worker route so a room owner can save edits before enqueuing a run.

Before the first publication, capture both currently serving Worker deployment
and version IDs. Each must serve one version at 100 percent. Retain the resulting
`meet-rollback-frontend-target.json` and `meet-rollback-realtime-target.json`
alongside the authorized release receipt. A historical pair alone is insufficient.

The workflow restores both captured versions if publication or smoke checks fail.
With the same captured receipts and approved credential context, the one-command
recovery is:

```sh
bash scripts/ci/meet-release-operations.sh restore
```

The helper verifies both serving versions after restoration. A failed release
remains failed and does not emit a success marker. Retain rollback and admission
results even when the deploy stops.

## Live acceptance

Check `/api/build-info` against the candidate and verify the frontend and realtime
deployment identities. Using a consent-qualified disposable account and an approved
empty meeting, verify opted-in Sorbet, the display-name and email/workspace footer,
login, logout and realtime connection. Do not use another person's signed-in
session for destructive account actions. Missing test custody is blocked/not run,
not a product failure. Capture signed-in navigation and request timings using the
[Meet loading contract](/platform/applications/meet#signed-in-list-loading).

## Canonical path cutover

Mount the qualified Meet Worker on `tuturuuu.com/meet` before redirecting legacy
document traffic.

### Prepare the cutover

1. Qualify the exact integrated commit with Meet's restored Worker artifact
   checks, the gateway Build Output checks, affected Web and mobile checks,
   and independent review of the mounted session, CSRF, CSP and Trusted Types.
   Use the [same-origin security gate](/platform/architecture/one-origin-security)
   before admitting public apex traffic. Verify the production guest Turnstile
   widget lists both `tuturuuu.com` and `meet.tuturuuu.com`. Retain both hostnames
   through rollback. Apply the same narrowly scoped Meet audio-upload WAF
   exception on the apex only if its predicate is verified for the mounted
   route. Match the exact host, POST, multipart content type and
   `/meet/api/meet-ai/*/*/chunks`.
2. Capture the current 100% version IDs and their binding inventories. Observe
   the serving version again immediately before each traffic change.

   ```sh
   cf workers deployments list --worker tuturuuu-meet
   cf workers deployments list --worker tuturuuu-meet-realtime
   cf workers deployments list --worker tuturuuu-gateway
   cf workers versions get "$OLD_MEET" --worker-id tuturuuu-meet
   cf workers versions get "$OLD_REALTIME" --worker-id tuturuuu-meet-realtime
   cf workers versions get "$OLD_GATEWAY" --worker-id tuturuuu-gateway
   ```

3. Use credential-free, exact-source cf Build Output for each Worker version.
   The Meet workflow seals Void output, and the
   [Void publisher](/build/development-tools/cf-cli-wrangler-parity#void-framework-app-publisher)
   converts that exact artifact to cf Build Output with the existing Asset,
   service, R2, Images and SQLite Durable Object bindings, the original
   migration tag and the full module inventory. Never add `exports` to Meet:
   it would make every captured rollback version undeployable.
   The gateway starts from the qualified gateway output with the captured
   serving bindings merged. Preserve the other mount entries, services and
   origin settings. Stage these variants in separate artifact directories.

   | Variant | Binding change |
   | --- | --- |
   | Meet shadow | `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET=shadow` |
   | Gateway mount | Add `MOUNT_MEET → tuturuuu-meet` and append `/meet,/meet/*` to `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS` |
   | Meet temporary | `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET=on`, `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET_REDIRECT_STATUS=302` |
   | Meet permanent | Same as temporary with `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET_REDIRECT_STATUS=301` |

   Preserve the existing apex gateway route and Meet custom domain. The
   redirects run in Meet's existing Worker. A realtime deployment is required
   only if the separately qualified release changes that Worker.

   Meet's release workflow reads the repository variables
   `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET` (`off`, `shadow` or `on`; default `off`) and
   `TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET_REDIRECT_STATUS` (`301`, `302` or `307`; default `302`)
   into every published version. Set them to each stage's value with
   `gh variable set` before or together with that stage's direct publication,
   so a later release keeps the stage instead of reverting it. Restoring a
   version does not change these variables: when rolling back a stage, set
   them to the restored stage's values as part of the rollback so the next
   release does not re-apply the withdrawn stage.

   For a Meet variant, emit the restored exact-SHA artifact with the variant's
   variables and publish it strictly:

   ```sh
   node scripts/ci/void-cf-output.mjs --config "$EMITTED_CONFIG" --out "$OUT" \
     --sha "$SOURCE_SHA" --var TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET=shadow \
     --var TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET_REDIRECT_STATUS=302
   node scripts/ci/void-cf-publisher.mjs publish --build "$OUT" \
     --worker tuturuuu-meet --message "$SOURCE_SHA" --strict > publish.json
   node scripts/ci/void-cf-publisher.mjs assign --worker tuturuuu-meet \
     --version "$(jq -er .versionId publish.json)" \
     --expect-current "$(jq -er .previousVersionId publish.json)"
   ```

   The gateway variant uses the steps below.

   Run these from each approved artifact directory. Record the version ID
   returned by the upload and read back its bindings before assigning traffic.

   ```sh
   cf workers versions create --prebuilt --mode production --dry-run --worker "$WORKER"
   cf workers versions create --prebuilt --mode production --worker "$WORKER" --message "$SOURCE_SHA"
   cf workers versions get "$VERSION" --worker-id "$WORKER"
   cf workers deployments create --worker "$WORKER" --strategy percentage \
     --versions "[{\"version_id\":\"$VERSION\",\"percentage\":100}]"
   cf workers deployments list --worker "$WORKER"
   ```

### Promote and verify

1. Deploy the Meet shadow version and verify old-host build identity before
   assigning traffic to the gateway version with the mount. Append `meet` to
   `NEXT_PUBLIC_TUTURUUU_ACTIVE_APP_MOUNTS` in the serving Web auth and shared
   link producers, including Mail and Meet's client build. Preserve other app
   entries. Keep mobile publishing after the apex smoke because its new share
   links default to the apex. The native collaboration WebView keeps the old
   host during the cutover.
2. Probe both frontend build-info URLs. Require HTTP 200, `app: meet`, the
   exact `commitHash`, production identity fields, `Cache-Control: no-store`,
   and `X-Gateway-Cache: MOUNT` on the apex response. Capture the response
   headers and serving version IDs together. A signed-in apex document must
   hand the browser `globalThis.__tuturuuuAppBase="/meet"`; an empty base sends
   the locale bundle and other runtime assets to the apex root. Check the bare path, the
   Vietnamese landing, route links, fingerprinted assets and fonts, and a
   server function requested by browser navigation. Compare cache headers on
   static assets and on a signed-in response.

   ```sh
   curl --fail --silent --show-error --dump-header - \
     'https://tuturuuu.com/meet/api/build-info'
   curl --fail --silent --show-error --dump-header - \
     'https://meet.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info'
   curl --fail --silent --show-error 'https://meet-realtime.tuturuuu.com/health'
   ```

3. With approved disposable identities, open a protected meeting link from a
   signed-out browser and complete Web login. Expect the exact mounted room or
   list URL, shared session, and no per-app session cookies at the apex. Check
   that a user from a different workspace cannot open a protected record.
   In a disposable room, join two clients with microphone and camera. Verify
   the join-token request, signaling upgrade, two-way SFU media, chat and
   reconnection. Exercise the authorized live-assistant socket if enabled.
   From another fresh browser, complete guest Turnstile and verify the guest
   receives and can use the room credential. Exercise guest leave and global
   sign-out separately. Preserve the `__Host-meet-guest` cookie's host-only
   rules, including its required root path. Meet's pending-invite cookie is
   scoped to `/meet` on the apex.
4. Promote the temporary version. Check the old root and encoded nested paths
   with duplicate query parameters, and check that the apex does not loop.

   ```sh
   curl --silent --show-error --dump-header - --output /dev/null \
     -H 'Accept: text/html' \
     'https://meet.tuturuuu.com/vi/plans/a%2Fb/?tag=1&tag=2'
   ```

   Expect a 302 with `Cache-Control: no-store` and location
   `https://tuturuuu.com/meet/vi/plans/a%2Fb/?tag=1&tag=2`. Recheck signed-in
   and guest join plus legacy machine traffic. Promote the permanent version
   only after acceptance and the rollback window agree with the captured
   release packet. Repeat the probe and require 301.

### Legacy traffic and rollback

The old host continues to serve WebSocket upgrades, non-document requests,
assets and worklets, `/api/*` (including automation and auth callbacks),
`/.well-known/*` (including the Parley runtime probe), `/_meet/*`,
`/_rum`, `/_next/*`, and localized or unlocalized `/verify-token` and
`/native-collaboration`. Existing sockets keep their connections.
`meet-realtime.tuturuuu.com` continues to serve signed-token room signaling,
channels, and collaboration for both frontend origins. Existing mobile links
can still resolve their original room, and Web's `/personal/meet?room=…`
mobile entry remains available.

Rollback starts by assigning 100% traffic to the captured Meet version or
the qualified shadow version to stop new redirects, and set
`TTR_ONE_ORIGIN_MEET` (and its redirect status) back to that version's values
so the next release keeps the rollback. Restore the captured
gateway version to withdraw `/meet` and `/meet/*`. Remove only `meet` from the
Web auth and link-producer mount lists and restore their prior serving builds
as needed. Restore realtime only if its version changed during this release.

```sh
cf workers deployments create --worker tuturuuu-meet --strategy percentage \
  --versions "[{\"version_id\":\"$OLD_MEET\",\"percentage\":100}]"
cf workers deployments create --worker tuturuuu-gateway --strategy percentage \
  --versions "[{\"version_id\":\"$OLD_GATEWAY\",\"percentage\":100}]"
cf workers deployments list --worker tuturuuu-meet
cf workers deployments list --worker tuturuuu-gateway
```

After a 301, browsers can retain the apex destination. If the failure allows
it, keep the qualified shadow version and gateway mount available to those
clients while restoring legacy navigation. If apex ingress must be stopped,
restore the previous gateway version immediately after disabling redirects.
Verify old-host identity, signed-in join and the realtime/SFU smoke after
rollback.
